items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Hamilton had a nice soft sound on clarinet... Yank also accompanied her... Teddy had a soft when touch on piano... I... was not as good when I had to play loud.

ctx.x: The other act was a young woman named Hazel Scott. Hazel was a classical pianist who would play a classical number as it was supposed to be played, and then do the same number in jazz. She was well trained and was also an arranger and jazz singer. Yank also accompanied her with wire brushes. In fact he played only wire brushes which sometime didn't give the band the push it needed on certain numbers.

We didn't play loud because it was not necessary. Teddy had a soft when touch on piano, Benny Morton was at his best/playing not too loud and so was I. That was the big difference in playing in a big band and a small combo. In a big band you must blow loud and my ideas and technique were not as good when I had to play loud. Hamilton had a nice soft sound on clarinet and was really an admirer of Benny Goodman. So Yank's brushing style was nice for the band except as I mentioned before, it didn't always give the…

Yank Porter had worked at a Cafe before. Teddy went in and as Yank was very well liked by Barney Josepson, Teddy was obliged to use him. And John Hammond had made pressure on him to hire me, although I had worked with Teddy in Benny Carter's orchestra, I know that he had another trumpet player in mind when I was pushed on him.
